manifest.name: CNC Machines
manifest.description: A CNC Machines tracker: spindle, axes, work area, controller, coolant. A named view of your machines, so each mill still drives jobs, fleet status, and maintenance.
manifest.author: Cobblr community
manifest.changelog: A group's summary adds up only what adds up: a length or a weight per item is totalled as length or weight times how many you have, and a year, a size or a temperature is no longer summed.

releases.notes: A group's summary adds up only what adds up: a length or a weight per item is totalled as length or weight times how many you have, and a year, a size or a temperature is no longer summed.
A dropdown says whether a value you type is remembered as a choice for next time; the open ones (a board, a firmware, a controller) offer what you typed before.
A CNC machine's page now uses its own words: it sends jobs to a job manager (the software that runs it, through your bridge), and asks only what fits a CNC machine.

Your CNC machines open the full machine page: set every field (spindle, axes, work area, controller, coolant), edit in place, attach files, and link the machine straight to its job manager right from its own page. Installing offers a checked-by-default “Connect to your CNC machines” option that brings the Job Manager along (send a file to be made and track the job), which you can uncheck for catalog-only use. Existing installs auto-upgrade: your CNC machines move into the CNC Machines tab automatically, no reinstall.

features.name: Connect to your CNC machines
features.question: Want to send files to your CNC machines and track the job?
features.description: Adds the Job Manager: map each machine to the software that runs it (the software that runs it, through your bridge), send a file to be made, and track the job to completion. Talks to the manager's API; it never drives the hardware. You can link a machine to its manager right from the machine's page.
